items.name: AA batteries, 4-pack
items.why: Powers the week 1 gate circuit, the two-LED meeting machine and the mBot through the season.

items.name: Counters for Nim (pennies or beans, household)
items.why: Week 1 winning positions on the table.

items.name: Electronics add-on pack (extra buttons and switches, LEDs, resistors, battery holder)
items.why: Sprint 1 needs several buttons at once for gates; the Season 1 kit has one.

items.name: Multimeter, basic
items.why: Turns test-it-or-trust-it into practice; they measure their own circuits before powering them.

items.name: small whiteboard and markers
items.why: For working out problems out loud and for the bug diary.

items.name: Helping hands or small PCB vise
items.why: Holds the board so both hands stay on the tools.

items.name: Kid-size safety glasses, two pairs
items.why: One for the child, one for the adult at the bench.

items.name: Perfboard pack and hookup wire
items.why: The permanent home for their gate badge.

items.name: Small wire strippers and pliers
items.why: Strips and shapes wire before soldering the badge circuit onto perfboard.

items.name: Soldering iron kit (temperature controlled, stand, lead-free solder, brass tip cleaner)
items.why: The week 5 milestone; adult supervised only.

items.name: Python 3 and a code editor on the laptop
items.why: Programs the mBot and processes the sensor log with real code, starting week 6; a free install done once with a grown-up.

items.name: Tape measure
items.why: Measures the mBot's stopping distance and the desk lamp's throw for the sensor log.

items.name: Black electrical tape and poster board (fresh line course)
items.why: Marks a brand new line course for the mBot creature, since season 1's course is already taped down and marked up.

items.name: Card stock and a paper fastener (household)
items.why: The week 7 Caesar wheel.

items.name: Cereal box and cardboard scraps
items.why: Builds the family's obstacle and a dim tunnel for the mBot's obstacle course.

items.name: Free build budget (cap set by owner; suggestion 40)
items.why: The real money exercise; they price the list themselves against the cap, the pay yourself first slice leaves first, and the shopping happens after the pitch's yes, purchased by week 10.

items.name: Protractor and compass set
items.why: Angles, triangle sums, build plan drafting.

items.name: Tri-fold science fair board
items.why: The week 11 board draft and the week 12 presentation.

items.name: Spring scale set (0 to 5 N and 0 to 20 N)
items.why: Measures lifting force for the lever, the gear train's output and the friction drag tests.

items.name: Small screw-eye hooks, 2-pack
items.why: Gives the spring scale a hook point on a test block and a lever arm.

items.name: String and two spools or a spool and a pencil (household)
items.why: Rigs the fixed and moving pulleys in the week 1 lever bonus.

items.name: LEGO Technic gear set (8, 16 and 24-tooth gears, axles and beams)
items.why: Builds the gear trains that trade speed for force and set up the output-arm force test.

items.name: Digital calipers
items.why: Measures a real part to a hundredth of a millimetre before it is modelled and printed.

items.name: 3D printer, a real fabrication machine (Bambu Lab A1 class: auto bed levelling, 0.1 mm layers, at least 180 by 180 mm bed, PLA and PETG)
items.why: Prints the parts the child designs from week 5 on to real dimensions: the mBot upgrades, brackets, gear and pulley parts, and in season 3 the servo mount and gripper. A machine in this class holds tolerances that let a printed part bolt onto the robot; a toy-grade printer does not, and the exercise would stop being engineering. The full A1 (256 mm bed) is the pick if a season 3 or 4 rover chassis will be printed in one piece.

items.name: PLA filament, 1 kg spool, plus one spool of PETG for load-bearing robot parts
items.why: PLA for every fabrication week's first print; PETG for the parts that carry a load on the robot, since PLA snaps where PETG bends.

items.name: Tinkercad account (free, browser CAD at tinkercad.com)
items.why: Models parts to real measured dimensions before they are printed.

items.name: Craft sticks, 100-pack
items.why: Builds the three truss designs for the load-to-failure test.

items.name: Hot glue gun and glue sticks
items.why: Joins the craft-stick truss; an adult stays at the bench while it is hot.

items.name: Small paper cups and washers or pennies (household)
items.why: A hanging load that adds weight gradually to test the truss and the printed part to failure.

items.name: KiCad (free schematic software at kicad.org), or paper and a printed circuit-symbol sheet
items.why: Draws a real circuit as a schematic with proper symbols instead of a breadboard photo.

items.name: Motor driver board (small H-bridge or transistor driver module)
items.why: Lets a micro:bit pin switch a motor's current without carrying it, and shows the driver as a switch.

items.name: Small DC hobby motor
items.why: The motor the driver board switches, measured at no load, light load and briefly stalled.

items.name: Two colours of counters or beads for Hex
items.why: The season 2 sprint 1 game, needed by week 1; the board itself is printed at no cost.

items.name: A deck of playing cards for Guess my rule
items.why: The season 2 sprint 2 game, needed by week 5; free if already in the house.

items.name: 24 Game card deck
items.why: The season 2 sprint 3 game, needed by week 9 (a regular deck of playing cards works free instead).

items.name: Digital probe or candy thermometer (reads to at least 100 C)
items.why: Confirms the water is hot enough before testing how a PLA scrap softens past its glass transition.

items.name: Bean seeds and two small cups of soil
items.why: A lit cup and a shaded cup let you watch what the light sensor's own number is doing for a living plant.
